_comments: Train ML Model — thin Action boundary over TrainingEngine.trainModel.
Type='Custom' + DriverClass binds to the @RegisterClass(BaseAction,'PredictiveStudioTrainModelAction') class.
The action validates PipelineID, delegates to the engine (production seams), and maps the result.

fields.Name: Train ML Model
fields.Description: Trains a predictive model from an ML Training Pipeline definition. Carves a locked holdout, trains via the sidecar, persists an immutable Draft ML Model, and flags single-feature dominance (possible target leakage). Outputs the new model id, its honest holdout metrics, and whether it was leakage-flagged.

fields.Name: PipelineID
fields.Description: Id of the MJ: ML Training Pipelines row to train.

fields.Name: MaxRows
fields.Description: Optional cap on the number of training rows pulled from the target entity.

fields.Name: ModelID
fields.Description: Id of the produced (Draft) MJ: ML Models row.

fields.Name: HoldoutMetrics
fields.Description: JSON of the metrics scored once on the locked holdout set the search never saw (the honest performance number).

fields.Name: LeakageFlagged
fields.Description: True when one feature dominates the model's predictions (possible target leakage). A flagged model stays Draft and needs human sign-off before promotion.
Model trained and persisted (Draft).
PipelineID is missing.
The training engine failed (pipeline not found, sidecar error, or a save failure).

_comments: Score Record Set — thin Action boundary over the MLModelInferenceProcessor scoring work type.
Validates ModelID + Scope, delegates scope resolution + scoring to the runner, returns counts +
ephemeral predictions OR confirms a write-back.

fields.Name: Score Record Set
fields.Description: Scores a set of records with a trained ML Model. The scope selects records (explicit ids / a saved view / a list / an entity+filter / a single record). Returns the scored count and either the ephemeral predictions or confirmation that scores were written back to the target.

fields.Name: ModelID
fields.Description: Id of the MJ: ML Models row to score with.

fields.Name: Scope
fields.Description: JSON describing the records to score. Populate exactly one of: records (id/pk array), viewId, listId, filter ({entityName, extraFilter, maxRows}), single ({entityName, primaryKey}).

fields.Name: WriteBack
fields.Description: Optional. true to write scores back with the model's default mapping, or an object { OutputMapping: ... } to write to a specific column/child record. When omitted, predictions are returned ephemerally.

fields.Name: ScoredCount
fields.Description: Number of records successfully scored.

fields.Name: WroteBack
fields.Description: True when scores were written back to the target (predictions are then NOT returned ephemerally).

fields.Name: Predictions
fields.Description: JSON array of ephemeral predictions ({recordId, score, class}), present only when WriteBack was not requested.
Records scored (predictions returned or written back).
ModelID is missing, or Scope is missing/empty/populates no selector.
Scope resolution or the scoring run failed (model/artifact not found, sidecar error).

_comments: Run Experiment Session — thin Action boundary over ExperimentOrchestrator.runSession.
Validates that an APPROVED PlanSpec is supplied, parses Budget + ExperimentID, delegates, maps the result.

fields.Name: Run Experiment Session
fields.Description: Executes an approved modeling plan as an experiment session — running its proposed experiments in waves to completion or until the budget bound, maintaining a leaderboard. Outputs the session id, the best (winning) model id, the final leaderboard, and why the session stopped.

fields.Name: PlanSpec
fields.Description: The approved modeling plan (ModelingPlanSpec JSON) to execute. Must have Approved=true — execution is gated on user approval.

fields.Name: ExperimentID
fields.Description: Optional id of an existing MJ: Experiments definition to attach the session to. When omitted, a new durable Experiment is created from the plan.

fields.Name: Budget
fields.Description: Optional budget override ({ MaxRuns, MaxComputeCost, MaxWallclockMinutes }). When omitted, the plan's ProposedBudget is used.

fields.Name: SessionID
fields.Description: Id of the MJ: Experiment Sessions row that was executed.

fields.Name: BestModelID
fields.Description: Id of the best (winning) model produced, or null when no iteration produced one.

fields.Name: Leaderboard
fields.Description: JSON of the final leaderboard, best-first ({ IterationID, Metric, ModelID }).

fields.Name: StopReason
fields.Description: Why the session stopped: completed, or a clean budget pause (budget-maxRuns / budget-maxComputeCost / budget-maxWallclock).
Experiment session ran to completion or paused cleanly on the budget.
PlanSpec is missing or not a valid modeling plan.
The PlanSpec is not approved (Approved is not true) — execution is gated on user approval.
The orchestrator failed during execution.

_comments: Promote ML Model — thin Action boundary over the model lifecycle transition.
Enforces the leakage sign-off gate: a leakage-flagged model is refused without SignOff=true.
Lifecycle-only — never edits metrics, only Status.

fields.Name: Promote ML Model
fields.Description: Transitions an ML Model through its lifecycle (Validated / Published / Archived). Enforces the leakage sign-off gate — a model flagged for possible target leakage cannot be promoted unless SignOff=true. Lifecycle-only: never edits the model's metrics or artifact, only its Status.

fields.Name: ModelID
fields.Description: Id of the MJ: ML Models row to transition.

fields.Name: TargetStatus
fields.Description: The lifecycle status to move the model to: Validated, Published, or Archived.

fields.Name: SignOff
fields.Description: Human/agent sign-off that overrides the leakage gate. Required (true) to promote a leakage-flagged model; ignored for clean models.

fields.Name: Status
fields.Description: The model's new lifecycle status, on success.
Model transitioned to the target status.
ModelID is missing, or TargetStatus is missing/not one of Validated/Published/Archived.
The model was flagged for possible target leakage and cannot be promoted without SignOff=true.
No ML Model exists with the provided ModelID.
The status transition failed to save.
An unexpected error occurred while promoting the model.

_comments: Schedule Model Scoring — thin Action boundary over the PS2-6 createScheduledModelScoring helper.
Schedules a trained ML Model to score a record scope on a recurring cadence. OutputField is OPTIONAL:
set it to write the prediction into that column (+ a scoring binding); omit for generic output (predictions
in the process run history only). Validates ModelID + TargetEntityName + exactly one scope selector,
delegates to the helper (which creates + saves a scheduled MJ: Record Processes row whose owned
MJ: Scheduled Jobs row is auto-created on save), and returns the new Record Process id + cron.

fields.Name: Schedule Model Scoring
fields.Description: Binds a trained ML Model to write its prediction into a target entity column on a recurring schedule (e.g. monthly). Creates a scheduled Record Process that scores the rows selected by a filter and writes the prediction back into the chosen column on its cadence. Outputs the new Record Process id and the cron expression.

fields.Name: ModelID
fields.Description: Id of the MJ: ML Models row to score with.

fields.Name: TargetEntityName
fields.Description: Name of the entity whose rows are scored and written (e.g. 'Memberships').

fields.Name: OutputField
fields.Description: Optional. The target-entity column to write the prediction into (e.g. 'RenewalScore'). Omit for generic output — each run records its predictions in the process run history (MJ: Process Run Details) only, with no write-back column and no scoring binding.

fields.Name: ScopeFilter
fields.Description: SQL predicate over the target entity selecting which rows each scheduled run scores (e.g. "Status='Active'").

fields.Name: Cadence
fields.Description: Recurrence: 'Monthly' (default — 1st of each month), 'Weekly', 'Daily', or a raw cron expression. When omitted, Monthly is used.

fields.Name: PrimaryKeyField
fields.Description: Primary-key field on the target entity (defaults to 'ID').

fields.Name: ValueKind
fields.Description: Which prediction value to write: 'score' (numeric probability/value — the default) or 'class' (predicted class label).

fields.Name: RecordProcessID
fields.Description: Id of the scheduled MJ: Record Processes row that was created (its owned MJ: Scheduled Jobs row is auto-created on save).

fields.Name: CronExpression
fields.Description: The cron expression the scoring run recurs on.
The scheduled scoring Record Process was created and saved (now live on its cadence).
A required param (ModelID / TargetEntityName / ContextUser) or the single scope selector is missing (OutputField is optional — omit for generic output).
The target entity was unknown, or the Record Process failed to save.

_comments: Browse ML Component Tree — the agent's read surface over the typed component model.
Reading the tree is not the same as reading a list of algorithms: a leaf's real capabilities are the
ones it INHERITS, so naming a ComponentTypeName returns the RESOLVED profile (merged banks, gates and
slots) WITH provenance, so an agent can say where a constraint came from rather than just that it exists.

fields.Name: Browse ML Component Tree
fields.Description: Explore the ML component catalog: list component types (optionally narrowed to one Kind), or resolve one type's full inherited profile — its effective preprocessing bank, hyperparameter bank, statistical gates and slots, each with the ancestor node that contributed it.

fields.Name: ComponentTypeName
fields.Description: Name of one component type to resolve in full (e.g. 'XGBoost'). When supplied, returns the resolved Profile instead of a list.

fields.Name: Kind
fields.Description: Narrow the listing to one Kind: Model, Preprocessing, Statistic, Input, Output, Parameter, or Structure.

fields.Name: ConcreteOnly
fields.Description: When listing by Kind, exclude abstract types (which exist to carry inherited properties and cannot be instantiated). Defaults to false.

fields.Name: ComponentTypes
fields.Description: The matching component types (id, name, kind, abstractness, parent, archetype story).

fields.Name: Profile
fields.Description: The resolved profile of the named type: its root-first inheritance Chain, effective Properties, Slots and per-key Provenance.
The tree was read.
No component type has that name.
The component tree could not be read.

_comments: Find Reusable Components — reuse by MEANING, not by name.
The caller supplies the query embedding deliberately: the component stories were embedded with a
specific model, and a vector from a different one yields distances that look like numbers and mean
nothing. Similarity is only half the answer — when ForComponentTypeID + ForSlotName are given, only
components the slot would LEGALLY accept survive, and unapproved/untrained components are excluded by
default so unreviewed work is never silently propagated into a new model.

fields.Name: Find Reusable Components
fields.Description: Find an already-trained ML component worth reusing, by what it means rather than what it is called. Ranks components by the similarity of their stories to a query embedding, and (optionally) keeps only those that can legally fill a named slot on a given component type. Approved, trained components only unless told otherwise.

fields.Name: QueryText
fields.Description: What you are looking for, in plain English — e.g. 'tells a real zero apart from missing data'. Embedded server-side with the same model that embedded the component stories, so the query and the catalogue are guaranteed to share a vector space. Supply this OR QueryVector.

fields.Name: QueryVector
fields.Description: The query embedding as a numeric array. Optional: prefer QueryText and let the server embed. When supplied it MUST come from the same embedding model the component stories were embedded with — a vector from a different model produces distances that mean nothing.

fields.Name: TopK
fields.Description: Maximum matches to return. Defaults to 10.

fields.Name: MinSimilarity
fields.Description: Minimum cosine similarity (0-1). Below this a match is noise dressed as a recommendation.

fields.Name: ForComponentTypeID
fields.Description: The component type whose slot is being filled. Must be supplied together with ForSlotName.

fields.Name: ForSlotName
fields.Description: The slot being filled. Only components the slot accepts (its Accepts type or a descendant) are returned.

fields.Name: PromotionStates
fields.Description: Promotion states to consider. Defaults to Approved only — reusing unreviewed work is not a default.

fields.Name: TrainedOnly
fields.Description: Only consider components with fitted state worth reusing. Defaults to true.

fields.Name: Matches
fields.Description: Ranked matches: instance id, name, component type, cosine similarity, the component's own story, and its promotion state.

fields.Name: CandidatesConsidered
fields.Description: How many components carried a usable story vector and survived the structural filter before ranking.

fields.Name: Warnings
fields.Description: Non-fatal notes — an unresolvable slot, components skipped for an unreadable story vector, or matches excluded because they cannot fill that slot.
The search ran (it may legitimately have found nothing).
The query vector was missing or malformed, or a slot filter was only half specified.
The reuse search could not complete.

_comments: Validate Component Graph — prove a proposed composition is buildable BEFORE anything trains.
Accepts either a bare Graph or a whole ArchitectureSpec, because the Architect produces the latter and
a human composing in the UI produces the former. Findings carry a path and a message that says what
WOULD have been valid, so a caller can fix its own proposal rather than guessing.

fields.Name: Validate Component Graph
fields.Description: Check a proposed ML component composition against the real component tree: every referenced type exists, none is abstract, each child fills a slot its parent actually declares, each filler is a type that slot accepts, required slots are filled and bounded ones are not over-filled. Returns per-node findings explaining what would have been valid.

fields.Name: Graph
fields.Description: The composition to check: a node of { ComponentTypeRef, SlotName?, Params?, Children? }. Either this or Architecture is required.

fields.Name: Architecture
fields.Description: A whole ArchitectureSpec; its ComposedGraph is validated. Either this or Graph is required.

fields.Name: Valid
fields.Description: True when the composition is buildable.

fields.Name: Findings
fields.Description: Per-node findings: severity, rule, dotted path, and a message naming what would have been valid.
The composition was checked (it may or may not be valid — see the Valid output).
Neither a Graph nor a usable Architecture was supplied.
The composition could not be checked against the tree.

fields.Name: Compute Signal
fields.Description: Compute ONE proven measure over a population — no model involved. Most business questions are measurements rather than predictions ('who has gone quiet since the conference?'), and running a whole model to answer one returns a probability where the asker wanted a number. Runs through the same feature-assembly path training uses, so the number matches what models were trained on. The optional binding parameters point a measure proven on one population at another: the signal's stored binding is a default, and anything supplied here replaces it while the meaning — the aggregate and its time window — stays fixed.

fields.Name: SignalID
fields.Description: The MJ: ML Components row to compute.

fields.Name: TargetEntity
fields.Description: Entity whose records are measured.

fields.Name: Filter
fields.Description: Optional filter narrowing the population.

fields.Name: MaxRows
fields.Description: Cap on records measured. Omitted measures the whole population.

fields.Name: AsOfColumn
fields.Description: Date column on the target entity. Each record's history is cut at ITS OWN value, which is what the signal was trained under. Omitted measures as of now.

fields.Name: SourceEntity
fields.Description: Binding override: entity holding the dated rows.

fields.Name: ForeignKeyField
fields.Description: Binding override: column referencing the target record's primary key.

fields.Name: DateField
fields.Description: Binding override: date column used to order and to cut the history.

fields.Name: ValueField
fields.Description: Binding override: value column for sum / avg / min / max / distinct count.

fields.Name: Column
fields.Description: Binding override: column name for a plain-column signal.

fields.Name: Values
fields.Description: One { RecordID, Value } per measured record.

fields.Name: OutputColumn
fields.Description: The column name the values were computed into.

fields.Name: ResolvedAs
fields.Description: What the signal actually measured after any override — entity, keys and window — for provenance.

fields.Name: List Signals
fields.Description: List the SIGNALS available — the individual proven measures models were built from, rather than the models themselves. This is where a caller gets the id that 'Compute Signal' needs, and it cannot be guessed. Supply QueryText to rank the catalogue by meaning ('how recently someone engaged' returns the recency measure, with no table or column name involved); omit it to list the catalogue in name order. Each entry says whether it is Rebindable — whether it can be pointed at a different population — which is resolved from the component tree rather than inferred, so a measure that carries its own execution path is never offered with a population picker beside it.

fields.Name: QueryText
fields.Description: Plain-English description of the measure wanted, embedded server-side with the same model that wrote the stories. Omitted, the catalogue comes back unranked in name order.

fields.Name: QueryVector
fields.Description: A pre-computed query embedding, as an alternative to QueryText. Must come from the SAME model the component stories were embedded with, or the distances are meaningless.

fields.Name: RebindableOnly
fields.Description: Hide measures that cannot be pointed at a different population. Defaults to false — they are still worth listing, just not rebinding.

fields.Name: MaxRows
fields.Description: Cap on entries returned. Defaults to 200.

fields.Name: MinSimilarity
fields.Description: Minimum cosine similarity for a ranked search, 0–1. Below it a 'match' is noise wearing a recommendation's shape.

fields.Name: PromotionStates
fields.Description: Review states to include. Defaults to every state — this is a catalogue, not a reuse proposal.

fields.Name: Signals
fields.Description: The catalogue: ID, Name, TypeName, Story, Rebindable, PromotionState, IsTrained, and Similarity when ranked.

fields.Name: Warnings
fields.Description: Non-fatal notes — measures excluded for not being rebindable, an unreadable story vector, an empty tree.

fields.Name: Find Relevant Findings
fields.Description: Search what this organization has actually LEARNED — dated, measured facts written when models were promoted, ranked by meaning. The counterpart to 'Find Reusable Components': that returns a measure you can run, this returns a fact you can cite. Every match carries its evidence type, magnitude, date, population size and out-of-sample metric, so a citation can be checked rather than trusted. Use MinEvidence to demand stronger evidence than an association — an agent recommending an ACTION should ask for 'Tested Intervention' and accept an empty answer rather than present a correlation as advice. An empty result means nothing has been measured about the question, NOT that the claim is false.

fields.Name: QueryText
fields.Description: Plain-English description of what you want to know ('why do members lapse?'), embedded server-side with the same model that wrote the finding stories.

fields.Name: QueryVector
fields.Description: A pre-computed query embedding, as an alternative to QueryText. Must come from the SAME model the finding stories were embedded with.

fields.Name: TopK
fields.Description: Maximum findings to return. Defaults to 10.

fields.Name: MinSimilarity
fields.Description: Minimum cosine similarity, 0-1. Below it a 'match' is noise wearing a citation's shape.

fields.Name: MinEvidence
fields.Description: Weakest evidence type to accept, from the ladder: Asserted, Descriptive, Observed Association, Predictive Contribution, Tested Intervention. Only the last supports 'if we do X, Y follows'.

fields.Name: TargetVariable
fields.Description: Restrict to findings about one outcome (e.g. 'Renewed').

fields.Name: IncludeSuperseded
fields.Description: Include earlier measurements of the same relationship — the historical chain that shows a lever moving. Defaults to false, so a caller gets the current state of knowledge.

fields.Name: Findings
fields.Description: The ranked findings, each with Statement, EvidenceType, Direction, Magnitude, Confidence, MeasuredAt, PopulationSize, the holdout metric behind it, and Similarity.

fields.Name: CandidatesConsidered
fields.Description: How many findings carried a usable story vector before ranking — the denominator separating 'nothing was close enough' from 'there was nothing to search'.

fields.Name: Warnings
fields.Description: Non-fatal notes — findings skipped for an unreadable vector, an unrecognized filter.

fields.Name: Assess Capability Coverage
fields.Description: Paste an organization's own strategic plan, funder report or board paper and get back what it can currently MEASURE, what it has actually LEARNED, and where neither is true. Coverage is reported on two axes because they come apart constantly and each combination implies different work: 'measurable but not yet studied' needs a study, 'known but not instrumented' needs instrumentation. IMPORTANT: a Gap means nothing on record DESCRIBES that objective — early in a deployment that is at least as likely to mean nobody has written the description as that the capability is missing, so the corpus sizes come back with every result and must be reported alongside any gap.

fields.Name: Text
fields.Description: The document to diagnose — a strategic plan, funder report or board paper. Cut into objectives deterministically (bullets and sentences, headings become sections), so the same document always produces the same diagnosis.

fields.Name: MaxObjectives
fields.Description: Cap on objectives extracted. Defaults to 60, so a long plan cannot become a thousand embedding calls.

fields.Name: StrongMatch
fields.Description: Similarity at or above which a match is treated as really being about the objective. Defaults to 0.55.

fields.Name: WeakMatch
fields.Description: Similarity at or above which something is 'close but not clearly it'. Defaults to 0.45.

fields.Name: TopK
fields.Description: How many signals and findings to return per objective. Defaults to 3.

fields.Name: Objectives
fields.Description: One entry per objective: the text, its section, the verdict (Covered / Measurable / Evidenced / Partial / Gap), the matching signals and findings with similarities, and the one-sentence next step.

fields.Name: Summary
fields.Description: Counts per verdict, for a headline.

fields.Name: SignalsConsidered
fields.Description: How many signals carried a usable story vector — the denominator behind every gap.

fields.Name: FindingsConsidered
fields.Description: How many findings carried a usable story vector.

fields.Name: Warnings
fields.Description: Non-fatal notes — an objective that could not be embedded, an empty corpus.
